title: Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators (ICDs)

criteria.text: Secondary prevention: sustained VT or VF arrest not due to acute MI or a transient/reversible cause
criteria.span: An episode of sustained VT, either spontaneous or induced by an electrophysiology (EP) study, not associated with an acute myocardial infarction (MI) and not due to a transient or reversible cause; or An episode of cardiac arrest due to VF, not due to a transient or reversible cause
Patients with a prior MI and a measured left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 0.30

criteria.text: Prior MI pathway: not NYHA class IV
criteria.span: New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification IV heart failure

criteria.text: Ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, NYHA II-III, LVEF <= 35%
criteria.span: Patients who have severe, ischemic, dilated cardiomyopathy but no personal history of sustained VT or cardiac arrest due to VF, and have NYHA Class II or III heart failure, LVEF ≤ 35%

criteria.text: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, NYHA II-III, LVEF <= 35%, optimal medical therapy for at least 3 months
criteria.span: Patients who have severe, non-ischemic, dilated cardiomyopathy but no personal history of sustained VT or cardiac arrest due to VF, and have NYHA Class II or III heart failure, LVEF ≤ 35%, been on optimal medical therapy for at least 3 months

criteria.text: Waiting periods (primary prevention): no CABG/PCI in past 3 months, no MI in past 40 days, not a revascularization candidate
criteria.span: Had an MI within the past 40 days

criteria.text: B2-B5: formal shared decision making with an evidence-based ICD tool before initial implant
criteria.span: a formal shared decision making encounter must occur between the patient and a physician

criteria.text: Familial/genetic high-risk disorder (e.g., long QT, HCM)
criteria.span: Patients with documented, familial or genetic disorders with a high risk of life-threatening tachyarrhythmias (sustained VT or VF), to include, but not limited to, long QT syndrome or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

criteria.text: Replacement for battery end of life, ERI, or device/lead malfunction
criteria.span: Patients with an existing ICD may receive an ICD replacement if it is required due to the end of battery life, elective replacement indicator (ERI), or device/lead malfunction
Patients must be clinically stable (e.g., not in shock, from any etiology)

criteria.text: All indications: LVEF measured by echo, nuclear imaging, cardiac MRI or catheter angiography
criteria.span: LVEF must be measured by echocardiography, radionuclide (nuclear medicine) imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or catheter angiography

criteria.text: All indications: no non-cardiac disease with likely survival under 1 year
criteria.span: Any disease, other than cardiac disease (e.g., cancer, renal failure, liver failure) associated with a likelihood of survival less than 1 year

criteria.text: All indications: no SVT such as AF with poorly controlled rate
criteria.span: Supraventricular tachycardia such as atrial fibrillation with a poorly controlled ventricular rate

notes: Shared decision making is required only for B2-B5 (primary prevention and genetic disorders), not for secondary prevention (B1) or replacements.
